debugging_guide.introduction: This guide provides comprehensive debugging strategies for Tkinter applications, particularly those integrating with AutoCAD via COM. It covers common issues, debugging techniques, and troubleshooting patterns.

issue.description: UI becomes unresponsive during long operations

symptoms.symptom: Window stops responding to user input
No progress updates during AutoCAD operations

root_causes.cause: Blocking AutoCAD COM calls in main thread

debugging_steps.step: Add timeout handling for COM operations
Verify AutoCAD is running and accessible
Validate parameter types and VARIANT conversions
Use try/catch blocks around all COM operations
Log HRESULT values for specific error diagnosis

issue.description: Threading issues causing deadlocks or race conditions

symptoms.symptom: Application hangs with no error messages

debugging_steps.step: Avoid accessing Tkinter widgets from background threads
Use daemon threads to prevent blocking on exit

issue.code_fix:
class ThreadSafeAutoCAD: """Thread-safe AutoCAD operations with proper synchronization."""
def __init__(self): self.com_lock = threading.Lock() self.ui_queue = queue.Queue() self.acad_app = None self.is_connected = False
def start_ui_updater(self, root): """Start thread that updates UI from background operations.""" def ui_updater(): while True: try: update_func = self.ui_queue.get(timeout=1) root.after(0, update_func) self.ui_queue.task_done() except queue.Empty: continue
updater_thread = threading.Thread(target=ui_updater, daemon=True) updater_thread.start()
def execute_thread_safe(self, operation, *args, **kwargs): """Execute AutoCAD operation in background thread.""" def background_operation(): try: # Update UI: operation starting self.ui_queue.put(lambda: self.status_var.set("Processing..."))
# Execute operation with COM lock with self.com_lock: result = operation(*args, **kwargs)
# Update UI: operation complete self.ui_queue.put(lambda: self.status_var.set("Complete"))
return result
except Exception as e: # Update UI: operation failed self.ui_queue.put(lambda: self.status_var.set(f"Error: {e}")) raise
# Start background thread thread = threading.Thread(target=background_operation, daemon=True) thread.start()
return thread
# Usage def safe_autocad_operation(self): def autocad_task(): # COM operations here are thread-safe if not self.autocad_manager.is_connected: self.autocad_manager.connect_autocad()
# Perform AutoCAD operations self.create_geometry()
self.autocad_manager.execute_thread_safe(autocad_task)

tool.name: tkinter_inspector
tool.usage:
# Enable Tkinter debugging root = tk.Tk() root.debug = True # Shows debug information
# Get widget information def inspect_widget(widget): print(f"Widget class: {widget.winfo_class()}") print(f"Widget geometry: {widget.winfo_geometry()}") print(f"Widget size: {widget.winfo_width()}x{widget.winfo_height()}") print(f"Widget position: {widget.winfo_x()}, {widget.winfo_y()}") print(f"Widget manager: {widget.winfo_manager()}")
if widget.winfo_manager() == 'grid': print(f"Grid info: {widget.grid_info()}") elif widget.winfo_manager() == 'pack': print(f"Pack info: {widget.pack_info()}")
# Inspect all widgets in a frame def inspect_frame(frame, indent=0): prefix = " " * indent print(f"{prefix}Frame: {frame}") for child in frame.winfo_children(): print(f"{prefix} Child: {child.winfo_class()}") if hasattr(child, 'winfo_children') and child.winfo_children(): inspect_frame(child, indent + 1)

tool.description: Monitor application performance and identify bottlenecks
tool.usage:
import time import psutil import threading
class PerformanceMonitor: """Monitor application performance."""
def __init__(self, root): self.root = root self.monitoring = False self.monitor_thread = None self.performance_data = []
def start_monitoring(self): """Start performance monitoring.""" self.monitoring = True
def monitor(): while self.monitoring: data = { 'timestamp': time.time(), 'cpu_percent': psutil.cpu_percent(), 'memory_percent': psutil.virtual_memory().percent, 'memory_mb': psutil.Process().memory_info().rss / 1024 / 1024, 'thread_count': threading.active_count() } self.performance_data.append(data)
# Update UI every second self.root.after(1000, lambda: self.update_performance_display(data))
time.sleep(1)
self.monitor_thread = threading.Thread(target=monitor, daemon=True) self.monitor_thread.start()
def stop_monitoring(self): """Stop performance monitoring.""" self.monitoring = False if self.monitor_thread: self.monitor_thread.join(timeout=2)
def update_performance_display(self, data): """Update performance display in UI.""" if hasattr(self, 'perf_label'): self.perf_label.config(text=".1f"
def get_performance_report(self): """Generate performance report.""" if not self.performance_data: return "No performance data available"
report = "Performance Report:\n" report += ".1f" report += ".1f" report += ".1f" report += f"Average threads: {sum(d['thread_count'] for d in self.performance_data) / len(self.performance_data):.1f}\n"
return report
# Usage monitor = PerformanceMonitor(root) monitor.start_monitoring()
# Later... print(monitor.get_performance_report()) monitor.stop_monitoring()

strategy.name: unit_testing_tkinter

troubleshooting_checklist.checklist_item: Verify AutoCAD is running before COM operations
Check COM initialization in each thread using COM
Use threading for long-running AutoCAD operations
Validate all input parameters before AutoCAD calls
Implement proper error handling and user feedback
Test layouts at different window sizes
Monitor memory usage and resource leaks
Test with both Real and Mock AutoCAD interfaces
Verify thread safety of all shared resources
